sub_graphs.title: EIP-6122: Fork ID Calculation and State Transition
sub_graphs.description: Models how nodes compute and update FORK_HASH based on block numbers and timestamps for network compatibility detection

nodes.label: Genesis Configuration Loaded
nodes.description: Node has loaded the genesis block hash and initial chain configuration

nodes.label: Compute FORK_HASH
nodes.description: Calculate IEEE CRC32 checksum by combining genesis hash with completed fork block numbers/timestamps in ascending order

nodes.label: FORK_HASH Computed
nodes.description: Node has a valid FORK_HASH representing all known completed forks

nodes.label: Determine FORK_NEXT
nodes.description: Identify the next upcoming fork block number or timestamp (0 if unknown)

nodes.label: ForkID Ready for Exchange
nodes.description: Complete ForkID (FORK_HASH + FORK_NEXT) is available for peer communication

nodes.label: Update Fork State on New Fork
nodes.description: When a new fork activates, recalculate FORK_HASH and FORK_NEXT values

edges.label: New fork activates at scheduled block/timestamp

external_entities.name: Chain Configuration
external_entities.description: External source providing fork schedule (block numbers and timestamps for each fork)

sub_graphs.title: EIP-6122: Peer ForkID Validation and Filtering
sub_graphs.description: Models how nodes validate incoming peer ForkIDs and decide to accept or reject connections

nodes.label: Remote Peer ForkID Received
nodes.description: Node has received a ForkID from a remote peer during handshake

nodes.label: Validate Peer ForkID
nodes.description: Compare remote ForkID against local chain configuration for compatibility

nodes.label: Peer ForkID Compatible
nodes.description: Remote peer's ForkID matches local expectations, connection may proceed

nodes.label: Remote Peer Stale
nodes.description: Remote peer has outdated fork information (ErrRemoteStale)

nodes.label: Local Incompatible or Stale
nodes.description: Local node is incompatible or stale compared to remote (ErrLocalIncompatibleOrStale)

nodes.label: Accept Peer Connection
nodes.description: Proceed with peer connection after successful ForkID validation

nodes.label: Reject Peer Connection
nodes.description: Disconnect from peer due to incompatible ForkID

external_entities.name: Remote Peer Node
external_entities.description: P2P network peer attempting to establish connection and exchanging ForkID

sub_graphs.title: EIP-6122: Fork Ordering Validation
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation rules ensuring timestamp-based forks are scheduled after block-based forks

nodes.label: Fork Schedule Loaded
nodes.description: Node has loaded the complete fork schedule from configuration

nodes.label: Validate Fork Ordering
nodes.description: Verify that all timestamp-based forks are scheduled at or after block-based forks

nodes.label: Fork Ordering Invalid
nodes.description: Fork schedule violates ordering constraint - timestamp fork before block fork

nodes.label: Filter and Sequence Forks
nodes.description: Process block-based forks before timestamp-based forks for checksum calculation

nodes.label: Deduplicate Fork Entries
nodes.description: Remove duplicate block numbers/timestamps at same height (checksum only once)

ambiguities.text: The specification mentions duplicate block numbers/timestamps are checksummed only once but doesn't clarify how duplicates at different logical forks are handled.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume duplicates refer to forks scheduled at the exact same block/timestamp and that only the first occurrence is used for checksum. This needs verification.

ambiguities.text: The specification doesn't explicitly define behavior when a node receives a ForkID with an unknown FORK_NEXT value.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume nodes should be tolerant of unknown future forks and only reject on confirmed incompatibility. This maintains forward compatibility.

implicit_assumptions.description: Nodes trust that the chain configuration source accurately represents the canonical fork schedule.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A malicious or incorrect chain configuration could cause nodes to reject valid peers or accept incompatible ones.

implicit_assumptions.description: The CRC32 checksum provides sufficient collision resistance for fork identification purposes.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Hash collisions could allow nodes with different fork configurations to appear compatible, potentially causing consensus splits.

implicit_assumptions.description: All nodes participating in the network have consistent fork schedules from genesis.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Nodes with inconsistent genesis configurations would be unable to connect to the main network.
